video_title: Is 'Bitcoin DeFi' Finally Taking Off — Except With Zcash and NEAR?
gist: Zcash and NEAR are rallying together (ZEC +32%/wk to CoinGecko #9, NEAR +69%/wk to #23) because NEAR Intents turns ZEC's shielded balances into a usable, cross-chain 'confidential DeFi' layer -- swaps, payments and perps settle privately across Bitcoin, Solana, Ethereum, Tron and more -- while Zcash's coming Ironwood/NU7 upgrade (quantum-proofing, 100x scale path, faster blocks) and a resolved Orchard counterfeit-mint vulnerability remove key overhangs.

themes.theme: Zcash/NEAR price action and what's really driving it

insights.claim: As of this taping, Zcash (ZEC) was up 32% on the week and ranked #9 on CoinGecko near an all-time high, while NEAR was up 69% on the week and ranked #23 -- both far outperforming Bitcoin and Ether's roughly 10% weekly moves.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Concrete, dated relative-strength data point for anyone tracking the privacy-coin/interoperability trade within this bull run.
insights.quote: Zcash is up 32% over the week. It's near an all-time high, and it's now ranked number nine on Coin Gecko... and Near is up 69% that time. It's now ranked 23

insights.claim: Mert Mumtaz argues privacy alone doesn't explain Zcash's rally, since Monero has pure privacy but hasn't seen comparable price performance -- the driver is the combination of Bitcoin-like scarcity narrative, quantum-security positioning, and privacy together, not privacy in isolation.
insights.speaker: Mert
insights.so_what: Suggests the ZEC trade is a multi-factor 'digital gold 2.0' narrative rather than a pure privacy-coin re-rating, which changes what would falsify or extend the thesis.
insights.quote: otherwise, for example, um you would have Monero as well doing the exact same price performance

insights.claim: Mert believes NEAR benefited from Zcash's rise, but that ZEC likely would not have appreciated as much without NEAR Intents giving it real spendable utility (wallet payments, cross-chain settlement) instead of just sitting idle on exchanges.
insights.speaker: Mert
insights.so_what: Implies the two assets are now reflexively linked -- NEAR's utility layer is becoming a structural bid for ZEC, worth monitoring for correlated flows.
insights.quote: it's questionable that Zcash would have went up as much if it weren't for near in the first place, giving it utility on the wallets

insights.claim: Ilia Polosukhin frames the rally as broader risk-on sentiment across crypto, with ZEC and NEAR simply being the tokens that outperformed the general market rather than moving for idiosyncratic reasons alone.
insights.speaker: Mert
insights.so_what: A reminder to separate beta (bull-market risk appetite) from alpha (the specific NEAR-Zcash utility thesis) when sizing this trade.
insights.quote: obviously people are more risk in general. Um and so all of crypto benefits and so you have to look at what outperforms the general market

themes.theme: Zcash + NEAR as the 'real Bitcoin DeFi'

insights.claim: The host's framing -- that Zcash plus NEAR Intents is effectively the long-promised 'Bitcoin DeFi' dream finally materializing, just not on Bitcoin or a Bitcoin layer 2 -- was endorsed by both guests as roughly correct.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Reframes the ZEC/NEAR trade as competing directly with the Bitcoin-L2/BTCfi narrative for capital and attention.
insights.quote: this is like the dream of Bitcoin DeFi actually coming true, just not on Bitcoin and not a Bitcoin layer 2, but with Zcash

insights.claim: NEAR led the effort to get ZEC listed and tradable on Solana via NEAR Intents, demonstrating the network's cross-chain routing/liquidity function in practice rather than just in theory.
insights.speaker: Mert
insights.so_what: A concrete, checkable milestone (ZEC-on-Solana listing) that investors can use to validate whether NEAR Intents adoption is actually expanding.
insights.quote: that was sort of for example, um we led the listing of Ze on Salana but via Near

insights.claim: Mert's framework: Zcash is 'a different Bitcoin' (store of value with added privacy/quantum-proofing), while NEAR is effectively what Ethereum's original sharding roadmap aimed to become -- a scaled, interoperable hub connecting other chains -- via NEAR Intents.
insights.speaker: Mert
insights.so_what: Positions NEAR as a direct narrative challenger to Ethereum's 'world computer/hub' thesis, using delivered interoperability as the differentiator.
insights.quote: who actually did that okay Near did and then what about sort of this being the hub where you connect different sort of chains well near is demonstra demonstrabably doing that right now

insights.claim: Ilia argues Bitcoin has stayed a 'pre-locked-in' ecosystem largely because it lacks privacy and is framed purely as a store of value, which reduces demand to interconnect with other chains; Zcash's shielded privacy creates demand to actually spend and participate in a broader DeFi economy.
insights.speaker: Ilia
insights.so_what: Suggests privacy is the missing catalyst that could pull dormant store-of-value capital into active DeFi use -- a thesis worth testing against on-chain ZEC activity vs. BTC activity.
insights.quote: Zcash by virtue of being private, people want to spend it. People want to kind of participate in economy around the world

themes.theme: Privacy as a retention and institutional-onboarding lever, not just a feature

insights.claim: Ilia's framework: privacy is not primarily an onboarding tool but a retention tool -- once users experience a private product, the reduced 'psychological anxiety' of not being tracked makes it very hard for them to go back to transparent alternatives.
insights.speaker: Ilia
insights.so_what: Implies privacy-enabled products should be judged on retention/LTV metrics rather than top-of-funnel growth, which changes how to value privacy-DeFi platforms.
insights.quote: it's not an on boarding tool it's a retention tool in a way... privacy actually brings I call it like a psychological safety

insights.claim: Mert counters that privacy is also a hard onboarding requirement for a specific but important minority -- institutions with regulatory obligations not to disclose customer information -- using a 'peanut butter allergy' analogy: a small population with an absolute blocker forces the whole system to add the option, even though most users don't need it.
insights.speaker: Mert
insights.so_what: Identifies regulated institutions as a distinct, high-value user segment whose on-chain participation is gated specifically on confidential settlement -- a segment to watch for institutional DeFi inflows.
insights.quote: there's always going to be people who have the limitation that they cannot come on chain unless they have some sort of uh private option. So institutions come to mind

insights.claim: Both guests acknowledge the classic privacy paradox -- users say in surveys they care about privacy but choose convenience in practice -- and argue the fix is building privacy as a seamless add-on to an already-better product, not asking users to trade convenience for privacy.
insights.speaker: Ilia
insights.so_what: A product-design lesson directly applicable to evaluating any privacy-crypto product's adoption curve: convenience-first UX predicts success more than privacy messaging.
insights.quote: generally people prefer convenience and then... you need to actually have a better product across the board

themes.theme: NEAR Intents mechanics, TVL and risk model

insights.claim: NEAR Intents TVL was reported at $190M on DeFiLlama with ZEC alone contributing $71M, but Ilia says DeFiLlama's figure misses the newly launched confidential balances -- the true combined TVL (non-confidential + confidential) is over $206M.
insights.speaker: Ilia
insights.so_what: Public TVL trackers may be materially understating NEAR Intents' actual scale because confidential-balance products aren't yet indexed -- worth re-checking DeFiLlama coverage before using it as the sole size metric.
insights.quote: the TVL is now over 200 uh 206 million and then uh I yeah I mean I think Zcash across both of them is yes 70 million

insights.claim: NEAR Intents works by users signing a desired trade ('intent') that is broadcast to competing solvers who bid quotes; the best quote settles through a 'verifier' smart contract and an MPC network that controls addresses on each external chain (Bitcoin, Solana, Zcash, etc.), replicating what centralized exchanges/custodians do but in a decentralized, programmable way.
insights.speaker: Ilia
insights.so_what: Explains the actual settlement mechanism investors are trusting when they route swaps through NEAR Intents -- MPC custody plus a solver auction, not a simple bridge.
insights.quote: we can effectively like what normally things centralized exchanges or even custodians do. They effectively put that on chain and we made it programmable

insights.claim: NEAR's 'confidential' tech stack (MPC + secure enclaves + zero-knowledge proofs) is deliberately different from Zcash's user-generated ZK proofs: Zcash has no shared computable state (limiting it to payments), whereas NEAR's private-shard nodes can compute over shared state, enabling fully programmable private DeFi -- trading, lending/earn, and perpetuals -- not just transfers.
insights.speaker: Ilia
insights.so_what: Clarifies the product differentiation thesis: NEAR is positioning as the programmable-DeFi complement to Zcash's pure store-of-value privacy, not a competitor to it.
insights.quote: we're leveraging a combination of multi-party computation, secure enclaves and zero knowledge groups... we call it confidential because indeed it's different from kind of more userfacing um privacies that Z uh Zcash is offering

insights.claim: Settlement can route funds directly into a Zcash shielded address, meaning a user can swap into or out of ZEC via NEAR Intents while the destination funds remain private end-to-end.
insights.speaker: Ilia
insights.so_what: A concrete product capability (shielded-address settlement) that differentiates NEAR Intents from typical cross-chain bridges for privacy-conscious users.
insights.quote: it can release it directly into Zcash shielded address. Right? So I can give it a shielded address directly

insights.claim: Ilia frames user risk on NEAR Intents as time-bounded: funds are only at risk of the MPC/bridge stack while a transaction is in flight between chains; once settled at the destination address, the user holds the asset natively with no ongoing counterparty exposure -- unlike opting into full confidential balances, which carries continuous exposure to the MPC/upgrade stack.
insights.speaker: Ilia
insights.so_what: A risk-assessment heuristic for anyone routing funds through NEAR Intents: transient bridging risk is lower than holding an ongoing confidential balance on the platform.
insights.quote: you're actually only taking risk while like in any of this component of the system while your funds are moving right so effectively as soon as they arrive to the destination address right you effectively done

insights.claim: NEAR runs an AI-driven monitoring/prevention system called 'Shield' that detects anomalous transactions and can pause a chain's activity; it triggered during a malicious Litecoin fork that exploited a privacy-pool double-spend, disconnecting that network from new NEAR Intents transactions until it stabilized, after only partial funds had moved through.
insights.speaker: Ilia
insights.so_what: A live incident showing NEAR's cross-chain security layer functioning proactively rather than reactively -- a relevant data point for assessing counterparty/bridge risk across the ecosystems NEAR Intents supports.
insights.quote: our systems detected that something is wrong and effectively disconnected that network and said like hey we're not going to... be accepting any new transactions for now until system stabilizes

insights.claim: NEAR has operated cross-chain custody infrastructure since 2021, starting with Rainbow Bridge, and claims to have never lost user funds across that history.
insights.speaker: Ilia
insights.so_what: A track-record claim investors should weigh when sizing bridge/MPC counterparty risk in NEAR Intents -- though it is self-reported and unaudited in this discussion.
insights.quote: We've been running like Rainbow Bridge was kind of the first version of this that we launched in 2021 and so we've been running this kind of systems for a a while now without losing any money

themes.theme: Zcash's Orchard counterfeit-mint vulnerability and its resolution

insights.claim: A vulnerability discovered in Zcash's Orchard shielded pool in mid-2026 could have allowed an attacker to mint counterfeit ZEC undetected, because in a fully shielded pool with no shared visible state, there is no way for any observer -- including the network itself -- to detect that inflation occurred.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Illustrates a structural risk unique to fully-anonymous protocols: undetectable supply inflation is possible precisely because privacy removes the ability to audit total state.
insights.quote: the orchard pool itself, since it's a fundamental pool or was a fundamental pool in Zcash, you could print new coins in there

insights.claim: Zcash fixed the Orchard counterfeit risk by migrating to a new 'Ironwood' pool with a turnstile mechanism enforcing that outputs cannot exceed inputs; over 90% of funds migrated (with forced migration triggered by any Orchard transaction), and the new design was formally verified three times to mathematically prove undetectable counterfeit bugs cannot exist.
insights.speaker: Mert
insights.so_what: Gives investors a concrete resolution timeline/mechanism to point to when assessing whether the Orchard vulnerability overhang on ZEC is actually closed.
insights.quote: it was formally verified three times over with also a new proof that shows that undetectable counterfeit bugs mathematically cannot exist

insights.claim: This class of vulnerability is specific to Zcash's fully-anonymous, no-shared-state architecture; other smart-contract platforms (including NEAR's private-shard model) retain internal monitoring/alerting nodes that can detect anomalies and retroactively patch issues, so a similar bug would not be fatal to those networks.
insights.speaker: Mert
insights.so_what: A differentiating risk factor between 'maximal privacy' chains and 'confidential-but-monitored' chains -- relevant to comparative risk-weighting of ZEC vs. NEAR-based private assets.
insights.quote: that's like a very specific problem to uh like an extremely anonymous protocol

insights.claim: Zcash's upcoming upgrade cuts block time from 75 seconds to 25 seconds, which Mert says will improve cross-chain settlement confidence and speed for NEAR interoperability specifically.
insights.speaker: Mert
insights.so_what: Faster ZEC block times directly reduce settlement latency/risk window for NEAR Intents swaps involving Zcash -- a concrete catalyst to watch for improved cross-chain UX.
insights.quote: the speeding up of block times from 75 seconds to 25 seconds, which will actually also help with uh near interoperability as well

insights.claim: The new Ironwood shielded pool uses a deliberately simpler ZK circuit design, which Mert argues reduces error surface and attack risk while also being the mechanism that both makes Zcash fully quantum-proof (versus merely quantum-recoverable today) and opens a path to scale the network roughly 100x.
insights.speaker: Mert
insights.so_what: Positions the Ironwood upgrade as Zcash's key de-risking and scaling catalyst -- a milestone to track for confirmation that the quantum-proofing and scale claims materialize.
insights.quote: it solves a problem that paves the road for Zcash to scale 100x but it also makes it fully quantum proof

insights.claim: Zcash's roadmap includes private on-chain governance -- coin holders privately voting/signaling on network decisions with 'skin in the game' -- which Mert describes as a primitive that doesn't exist in most other protocols.
insights.speaker: Mert
insights.so_what: Private governance could become a novel differentiator/feature to track as a leading indicator of Zcash's broader privacy-tooling roadmap maturing beyond payments.
insights.quote: coin holders can actually privately vote which by the way is not a primitive that exists many places

themes.theme: Formal verification and AI-driven security as the new DeFi security bar

insights.claim: Ilia argues the old security paradigm -- code is considered secure once 'smart people looked at it and wrote a PDF about it' -- is breaking down because AI now lets anyone deploy high-caliber automated code review, making formal verification a near-mandatory requirement for critical crypto software going forward.
insights.speaker: Ilia
insights.so_what: A forward-looking industry standard shift: protocols without formal verification may increasingly be viewed as under-secured relative to AI-era attacker capability, which could become a due-diligence checklist item for evaluating DeFi protocols.
insights.quote: the paradigm where before code was secure if some smart people looked at it and wrote a PDF about it is kind of starting to um disappear

insights.claim: NEAR published benchmark results claiming its formal-verification approach runs roughly 250x cheaper than existing market tooling (including traditional OpenAI-based systems), and says it can be run directly during development to verify properties like no double-spends and no value-extraction bugs.
insights.speaker: Ilia
insights.so_what: If accurate, a large cost reduction in formal verification could make it economically viable for far more DeFi protocols to adopt as a standard practice, potentially reducing the frequency of exploit-driven losses across the sector.
insights.quote: we can do 250 times cheaper for modification than what's right now in the market... with kind of traditional like uh open AI uh systems

themes.theme: Real-world privacy use case: high-net-worth travel opsec

insights.claim: Mert says he regularly uses ZEC settled through NEAR Intents to pay a 'private concierge' for travel bookings (flights, hotels, taxis) rather than using traceable USDT-on-Tron, specifically to prevent the payee from inferring his net worth from on-chain address history and using it to upsell him.
insights.speaker: Mert
insights.so_what: A concrete, real (not hypothetical) demand case for confidential settlement among high-net-worth crypto users -- evidence that privacy-enabled payment rails have working product-market fit beyond speculation.
insights.quote: my private concierge knows how much money I make and therefore now they're going to upsell me on all these sort of different shit

insights.claim: Most crypto merchants and travel intermediaries currently accept USDT on Tron rather than Zcash directly, so private settlement in practice often routes ZEC through NEAR Intents into USDT-on-Tron at the point of sale rather than merchants accepting ZEC natively.
insights.speaker: Mert
insights.so_what: Highlights a real adoption bottleneck: even with private settlement rails available, last-mile merchant acceptance still runs through Tron/USDT, capping how private the full payment chain actually is today.
insights.quote: most of the folks who deal in crypto, for whatever reason, they already take USDT on Tron
